Question B-003-012-010.

Why the correct answer is right: Lower sideband places the tone below the displayed carrier setting; 1000 Hz is 1 kHz, so 7100 kHz - 1 kHz = 7099 kHz.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "7099 kHz": This is the correct choice because lower sideband places the tone below the displayed carrier setting; 1000 Hz is 1 kHz, so 7100 kHz - 1 kHz = 7099 kHz.
- sourceIndex 1: "7101 kHz": That is the upper-sideband result: 7100 kHz + 1 kHz. Lower sideband subtracts the audio frequency.
- sourceIndex 2: "6100 kHz": This subtracts 1000 kHz instead of 1000 Hz. The tone is 1 kHz, so the shift is only 1 kHz.
- sourceIndex 3: "8100 kHz": This adds 1000 kHz instead of subtracting 1 kHz; it confuses hertz with kilohertz and the sideband direction.
